```{r Load clean_names_lowercase function}
clean_names_lowercase <- function(x) {

  x <- iconv(x, from = "", to = "UTF-8", sub = "")
  x <- stringi::stri_trans_general(x, "Latin-ASCII")

  x %>%
    tolower() %>%
    trimws()
}
```

# Join all goal dataframes:

## Long:
```{r}

Index_Scores_long0 <- bind_rows(
  AO_Scores,
  BD_Scores,
  CW_Scores,
  HS_Scores,
  FP_Scores,
  FIS_Scores,
  MAR_Scores,
  LE_Scores,
  NP_Scores,
  SP_Scores,
  TR_Scores
) %>%
  arrange(year, rgn_id, goal) %>%
  filter(!is.na(rgn_id),
         year>= 2005,
         year<= 2025)

colnames(Index_Scores_long0)

# Coalesce score values:
Index_Scores_long <- Index_Scores_long0 %>%
  mutate(
    goal_score = coalesce(
      AO_score,
      BD_score,
      CW_score,
      HS_score,
      FP_score,
      LE_score,
      NP_score,
      SP_score,
      TR_score
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    year,
    rgn_id,
    goal,
    goal_score
  ) %>%
  arrange(year, rgn_id, goal)

```

# GAP FILL:
Rules:
(1) If data (per region) is missing between two years where there is data available, interpolate the value. 
(2) If data (per region) is missing and is not surrounding by data before and after, take the most recent (previous) datapoint.

I.e.,
Internal gaps: linearly interpolate between the nearest available values before and after the missing year.
Leading gaps: if there is no later value and no earlier value surrounding the gap, carry the most recent previous value forward.
Don't use future values to fill a missing value when there is no previous observation.

```{r Gapfill the Index_scores_wide}
score_cols <- c(
  "LE_score", "CW_score", "AO_score", "FP_score", "NP_score",
  "BD_score", "SP_score", "TR_score", "HS_score"
)

Index_Scores_gapfilled <- Index_Scores_wide %>%
  filter(year >=2018, year <=2025) %>%
  filter(!is.na(OHI_region_no)) %>%
  arrange(OHI_region_no, year) %>%
  group_by(OHI_region_no) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(score_cols),
      ~ {
        x <- .x
        interp <- na.approx(x, x = year, na.rm = FALSE)
        na.locf(interp, na.rm = FALSE)
      },
      .names = "{.col}_Score"
    ),
    across(
      all_of(score_cols),
      ~ {
        x <- .x
        interp <- na.approx(x, x = year, na.rm = FALSE)
        filled <- na.locf(interp, na.rm = FALSE)

        case_when(
          !is.na(x) ~ "observed",
          !is.na(interp) ~ "interpolated",
          !is.na(filled) ~ "carried_forward",
          TRUE ~ NA_character_
        )
      },
      .names = "{.col}_provenance"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(
    OHI_region_no,
    year,
    unlist(
      lapply(
        score_cols,
        function(x) c(
          x,
          paste0(x, "_provenance")
        )
      )
    )
  )
# 72 obs., 20 vars.
```

```{r Calculate final (gapfilled) score}
colnames(Index_Scores_gapfilled)

Index_Scores_gapfilled <- Index_Scores_gapfilled %>%
  mutate(
    Index_score_gapfilled = rowMeans(

  )
```

```{r TESTING AN IDEA Nov 2026}

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)

set.seed(123)

# Time axis
time <- seq(0, 100, length.out = 500)

# a. Long-term climate variability
long_term <- sin(time / 12) * 0.8 +
  sin(time / 25) * 0.3

# b. Short-term weather variability
short_term <- rnorm(500, 0, 0.25)

# Add occasional extreme weather events
extremes <- rep(0, 500)
extreme_indices <- sample(1:500, 15)

extremes[extreme_indices] <- sample(
  c(-1.5, 1.5, -2, 2),
  15, replace = TRUE
)

weather <- short_term + extremes

# c. Climate change (gradual warming trend)
climate_change <- 0.01 * time

# d. Experienced weather
experienced <- climate_change + weather

# e. Population response
population <- rep(100, 500)

for (i in 2:500) {
  # Natural population recovery
  population[i] <- population[i-1] +
    0.04 * (100 - population[i-1])

  # Negative effects of extreme events
  if (experienced[i] > 1.5) {
    population[i] <- population[i] - 15
  }

  if (experienced[i] < -1.5) {
    population[i] <- population[i] - 10
  }
}

population <- pmax(population, 0)

# Combine data
df <- data.frame(
  time,
  long_term,
  weather,
  climate_change,
  experienced,
  population
)

# Common theme
theme_fig <- theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold", hjust = 0
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(8, 8, 8, 8)
  )

# Panel a: Long-term variability
p1 <- ggplot(df, aes(time, long_term)) +
  geom_line(color = "#4A9B65", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "a  Long-term climate variability") +
  theme_fig

# Panel b: Short-term weather variability
p2 <- ggplot(df, aes(time, weather)) +
  geom_line(color = "#D65A4A", linewidth = 0.6) +
  labs(title = "b  Short-term weather variability") +
  theme_fig

# Panel c: Climate change
p3 <- ggplot(df, aes(time, climate_change)) +
  geom_line(color = "#4682B4", linewidth = 0.9) +
  labs(title = "c  Climate change") +
  theme_fig

# Panel d: Experienced weather
p4 <- ggplot(df, aes(time, experienced)) +
  geom_rect(
    aes(
      xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf,
      ymin = 1.5, ymax = 3
    ),
    fill = "#E88B91", alpha = 0.35,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_rect(
    aes(
      xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf,
      ymin = -1.5, ymax = 1.5
    ),
    fill = "#E8C95A", alpha = 0.25,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = c(-1.5, 1.5),
    linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40"
  ) +
  geom_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
  labs(title = "d  Experienced weather") +
  theme_fig

# Panel e: Population size
p5 <- ggplot(df, aes(time, population)) +
  geom_line(color = "#8B65A5", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "e  Population size") +
  theme_fig

# Combine panels
(p1 | p2) /
(p3 | p4) /
p5 +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1, 0.8))

# Save
ggsave(
  "harris_figure1_recreated.png",
  width = 12,
  height = 10,
  dpi = 300
)

```

```{r Cont...}
library(ggplot2)

x <- seq(-4, 4, length.out = 1000)

# Individual distributions
long_term <- dnorm(x, mean = 0, sd = 1)
short_term <- dnorm(x, mean = 0, sd = 0.5)

# Combined distribution
combined <- dnorm(
  x,
  mean = 0,
  sd = sqrt(1^2 + 0.5^2)
)

df <- data.frame(
  x,
  long_term,
  short_term,
  combined
)

ggplot(df, aes(x)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = long_term, colour = "Long-term variability")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = short_term, colour = "Short-term variability")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = combined, colour = "Combined variability"),
            linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
    "Long-term variability" = "forestgreen",
    "Short-term variability" = "orange",
    "Combined variability" = "black"
  )) +
  labs(x = "Environmental conditions",
       y = "Probability density",
       colour = NULL) +
  theme_classic()
```

```{r Stats}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)


# Define components
predictor_vars <- c(
  "BD_score", "CW_score", "HS_score"
)

other_vars <- c(
  "LE_score", "AO_score", "FP_score",
  "NP_score", "SP_score", "TR_score"
)

df <- Index_Scores_wide %>%
  mutate(
    OtherScore = rowMeans(
      pick(all_of(other_vars)),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    OtherScore = if_else(
      is.nan(OtherScore),
      NA_real_,
      OtherScore
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(rgn_id, year) %>%
  group_by(rgn_id) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(predictor_vars),
      ~ if_else(
        year - lag(year) == 1,
        .x - lag(.x),
        NA_real_
      ),
      .names = "d_{.col}"
    ),
    d_OtherScore = if_else(
      year - lag(year) == 1,
      OtherScore - lag(OtherScore),
      NA_real_
    ),
    next_d_OtherScore = lead(d_OtherScore)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

model1 <- feols(
  next_d_OtherScore ~
    d_BD_score +
    d_CW_score +
    d_HS_score +
    d_OtherScore |
    rgn_id + year,
  data = df,
  cluster = ~rgn_id
)

summary(model1)

# H1: Nature-related dimensions (BD, CW, HS) exhibit slower rates of improvement than other dimensions.
# H2: The slower rate of improvement in nature-related dimensions constrains the rate of improvement in the overall index.

# First, are nature related changes more slow moving?
score_vars <- c(
  "BD_score", "CW_score", "HS_score",
  "LE_score", "AO_score", "FP_score",
  "NP_score", "SP_score", "TR_score"
)

change_summary <- df %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      starts_with("d_"),
      ~ mean(abs(.x), na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )

change_summary

# The mean annual improvement in the other dimensions is approximately:
# 5.7 times the biodiversity improvement.
# 12.6 times the habitat improvement.
# 2.2 times the climate/water improvement.

nature_vars <- c(
  "BD_score", "CW_score", "HS_score"
)

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    NatureScore = rowMeans(
      pick(all_of(nature_vars)),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    NatureScore = if_else(
      is.nan(NatureScore),
      NA_real_,
      NatureScore
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(rgn_id, year) %>%
  group_by(rgn_id) %>%
  mutate(
    d_Nature = if_else(
      year - lag(year) == 1,
      NatureScore - lag(NatureScore),
      NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# How are the nature variables changing compared to the others?
df %>%
  summarise(
    Nature_change = mean(d_Nature, na.rm = TRUE),
    Other_change = mean(d_OtherScore, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Is this difference significant?

comparison <- df %>%
  select(rgn_id, year, d_Nature, d_OtherScore) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(d_Nature),
    !is.na(d_OtherScore)
  )

t.test(
  comparison$d_OtherScore,
  comparison$d_Nature,
  paired = TRUE
)

# What's driving the decline?
df %>%
  summarise(
    BD = mean(d_BD_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    CW = mean(d_CW_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    HS = mean(d_HS_score, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
# Habitat
```
